Hi Oliver / Maya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation. Per our spot check, attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and the evaluation manifest for the pilot assets we discussed. High level ask: confirm the MAP and security constraints below so we can start provisioning a two-week sandbox access window and issue ephemeral tokens for the prompt pack.

Key pieces in this exchange (short):
- Artifacts we will provide: evaluation corpus (CSV manifest), prompt pack (ephemeral archive), and a small set of guarded testcases (JSON snippets).
- Usage constraints: evaluation-only, no model training/weight updates, no broad redistribution. Artifacts are watermarked and telemetry-enabled.
- Access model: ephemeral access tokens scoped to project, 30-day retention for logs, 30-day data expiry for uploaded customer signals.
- Timeline (proposed):
  1) Tue 3/16: Finalize MAP + security addendum
  2) Wed 3/17: DocuSign signature & provisioning trigger
  3) Thu 3/18: Sandbox access (canary) goes live for 2 weeks
  4) Mon 4/1: Review checkpoint & decide on expansion or handback

Attachments (stubs): [pilot_eval_manifest.csv (CSV)], [mpa-draft-integral.docx (DOCX)], [redwood-map-v1.0.pdf (PDF)].

Please review the MAP doc and the usage covenant paragraph on page 2 — I flagged the clause that says "no training or model fine-tuning with provided artifacts". If your legal needs stronger language around retention or revocation, ping me and I will have Karthik add security-addendum text.

Also here are the links: HubSpot deal and the shared folder (Drive) with the sample manifest and upload checklist. We can attach a short SSO/KMS questionnaire after signature if you'd like.

Next step: can you confirm by EOD Mon whether the timeline works? If yes, I will issue the DocuSign envelope and loop in our security contact.

Thanks,

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. Quick questions from procurement/legal and our data team before we sign:

1) Retention: your note says 30 days for logs and customer signals — can you confirm that the evaluation corpus and prompt pack will be purged (and a purge certificate issued) at handback? Our counsel prefers a signed destruction acknowledgement.
2) Masking: are the artifacts pre-masked or do you expect us to sanitize PII before uploading? We have some internal rules that dictate no raw PII leaves our environment.
3) Escrow: is there an option to hold a locked checksum/escrow of artifacts with a neutral third party (briefly) in case of disputes?

If you can address those points and include a short security contact, we can likely sign Wed and trigger provisioning Thursday.

Hi Oliver — looping in to address the security-specific items. TL;DR: yes to purge certificates and masking guidance; we can support escrow checks for checksum-only custody. Details below.

Retention and purge
- Redwood will issue a machine-signed purge certificate at handback confirming deletion of provided evaluation artifacts from our sandbox environment and from any short-term caches. Purge certificate will be a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums.
- System logs (access tokens, provisioning events) retained for 30 days by default; retention can be shortened to 14 days for this pilot if you prefer.

Masking / PII
- We strongly recommend you push pre-masked artifacts where possible. We provide a light-weight PII redaction checklist in the Drive folder; if you want, we can run an automated redaction pass in a staging pipeline but that requires a short onboarding job and an additional NDA addendum.

Escrow / checksum custody
- We can support a neutral checksum escrow: Redwood will generate and share SHA256 checksums for the artifacts at time of upload; if desired, we can deposit the list with a third-party notary service (example: NotaryCo) for the duration of the pilot. This is strictly checksum custody — we do not place your raw payload in escrow.

Usage constraints (enforcement)
- Contract language: "Evaluation-only; no training or derivative model creation permitted with provided assets." We will add a telemetry trigger that alerts both parties on any export-like activity.
- Prompt packs will be ephemeral, watermarked (metadata token), and accessible only via scoped ephemeral tokens; they cannot be downloaded wholesale by default.

Attachments: security-evidence-snapshot.pdf (stub).

If that looks good I can drop a short security addendum paragraph into the MPA and Ben can resend for signature.

—Karthik
